chunk_findings.detail: The replacement prints every `FAILED tests/test_x.py::…` line while scanning `"$@"` (or in the `named=0` loop) and then emits `=== short test summary info ===` with no FAILED lines under it. The previous fixture put those lines after that marker. A parser that only harvests the short-summary section (the usual pytest contract, and what this stub previously modeled) now sees zero node ids on both the full run and a named baseline run. Given `n=10` and `bin/pytest tests/test_x.py::test_a0 tests/test_x.py::test_a1`, evidence.baseline stays empty — the same failure mode as B69d1c0ff00 — so the regression does not exercise auto-accept.

chunk_findings.detail: Even if FAILED lines were collected from the whole stream, the stub always prints `{n} failed in 0.1s` and `exit 1`. On a baseline invocation that names a proper subset (the comment’s “fixed list”), the summary count is the full suite size, not the number of FAILED lines. A count-vs-list check, or a baseline that stores the summary total, records 10 failures for two named ids and will not match the item run.
